items.stem: Which of the following muscles in the sole of the foot is not supplied by the medial plantar nerve?
options: Flexor digitorum brevis
Flexor digiti minimi brevis
Flexor hallucis longus
Abductor hallucis
Flexor hallucis brevis
items.explanation:
The muscles of the sole of the foot can be arranged in four layers, consisting of the following pattern at the four layers: three muscles, two muscles and two tendons, three muscles, and two muscles and two tendons.

Layer 1: Flexor digitorum brevis (medial plantar nerve), abductor hallucis (medial plantar nerve) and abductor digiti minimi (lateral plantar nerve) Layer 2: Quadratus plantae (lateral plantar nerve), lumbricals (shared between medial and lateral plantar nerves like the hand), and the tendons of hallucis longus and flexor digitorum longus Layer 3: Flexor hallucis brevis (medial plantar nerve), adductor hallucis (lateral plantar nerve) and flexor digiti minimi brevis (lateral plantar nerve) Layer 4: Dorsal and plantar interossei muscles (lateral planter nerve) and the tendons of tibialis posterior and peroneus longus

items.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the posterior cruciate ligament is correct?
options: It is attached to the lateral femoral condyle.
It is made up of three separate bundles.
It prevents posterior dislocation of the tibia.
It plays no role in resisting hyperextension.
It is intrasynovial.
items.answer_text: It prevents posterior dislocation of the tibia.
items.explanation: The posterior cruciate ligament is attached to the lateral surface of the medial femoral condyle and extends down to the posterolateral aspect of the tibia. The ligament is made up of two separate bundles which, in turn, resist hyperextension and hyperflexion. The ligament’s main role is to restict posterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur. The ligament is extrasynovial but intracapsular.

items.stem: Which one of the following is the main function of the psoas major muscle?
options: Flexes the thigh at the hip joint
Extends the thigh at the hip joint
Adducts the thigh at the hip joint
Abducts the thigh at the hip joint
Assists in the full contraction of the diaphragm
items.answer_text: Flexes the thigh at the hip joint
items.explanation: The psoas major muscle joins the iliacus muscle, which originates broadly over the inner aspect of the iliac wing of the pelvis. This becomes the iliopsoas tendon and inserts on the lesser trochanter of the femur and thus flexes the thigh at the hip joint.

items.stem: A 31-year-old patient develops a common peroneal nerve palsy after treatment with a below-knee cast for 6 weeks for an undisplaced ankle fracture following a fall. Which one of the following statements regarding clinical examination is true?
options: The patient is unable to stand on tiptoe.
There would be complete sensory loss below the knee.
There would be no dorsiflexion of the foot.
The patient would complain of complete sensory loss on the sole of the foot.
Sensation would be normal on the dorsum of the foot.
items.answer_text: There would be no dorsiflexion of the foot.
items.explanation: The common peroneal nerve can be compressed by a below-knee cast at the level of the neck of the fibula. It supplies the muscles of the anterior and lateral compartments of the leg, producing dorsiflexion of the foot, ankle and toes, as well as eversion of the foot. The superficial peroneal nerve gives sensory supply to most of the dorsum of the foot. The deep peroneal nerve supplies the first web space.

items.stem: Moving from lateral to medial, which of the following describes the order of the structures in the femoral triangle?
options: Femoral vein, femoral artery, femoral nerve
Femoral nerve, femoral vein, femoral artery
Femoral nerve, femoral artery, femoral vein, long saphenous vein
Long saphenous vein, femoral vein, femoral artery, femoral nerve
Short saphenous vein, femoral vein, femoral artery, femoral nerve
items.answer_text: Femoral nerve, femoral artery, femoral vein, long saphenous vein
items.explanation: From lateral to medial, the femoral triangle contains the femoral nerve and its branches, the femoral artery and its branches, including the profunda femoris, and the femoral vein with its main tributary, the long saphenous vein.

items.stem: Which of the following muscles is not present in the anterior compartment of the leg?
options: Tibialis anterior
Extensor hallucis longus
Extensor digitorum longus
Peroneus tertius
Peroneus brevis
items.explanation: The muscles of the anterior compartment of the leg are tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus and peroneus tertius. They are all supplied by the deep peroneal nerve and receive their blood supply from the anterior tibial artery. Peroneus brevis is found in the lateral compartment of the leg, along with peroneus longus.

items.stem: Following open reduction and internal fixation of both the distal tibia and the distal fibula, a patient complains of numbness along the lateral side of the foot. Which nerve is likely to have been injured?
options: Sural nerve
Saphenous nerve
Deep peroneal nerve
Superficial peroneal nerve
Tibial nerve
items.explanation: The sural nerve arises from the tibial nerve. It is purely sensory and supplies the lateral border of the leg and the lateral border of the foot. It lies approximately 1 cm posterior to the distal fibula and may be damaged during operations on the distal fibula. The saphenous nerve supplies the medial aspect of the leg up to the medial malleolus.

items.stem: Multiple structures are contained within or pass through the popliteal fossa. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The popliteal vein becomes the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.
The short saphenous vein is the deepest structure within the fossa.
The popliteal artery is initially lateral to the tibial nerve, then moves medially when travelling distally though the popliteal fossa.
The short saphenous vein drains into the femoral vein.
The popliteal artery is formed from the profunda femoris.
items.answer_text: The popliteal vein becomes the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.
items.explanation: The popliteal fossa contains the short saphenous vein, which drains into the popliteal vein. The popliteal vein ends at the adductor hiatus where it becomes the femoral vein. The popliteal artery is the deepest structure within the fossa, initially lying medial to the tibial nerve and moving more lateral to it as it travels distally. The popliteal artery is a branch of the superficial femoral artery.

items.stem: Which of the following structures does not enter the adductor canal?
options: Femoral artery
Femoral vein
Nerve to adductor longus
Nerve to vastus medialis
Saphenous nerve
items.explanation: It begins at the apex of the femoral triangle and ends at the adductor hiatus. Contents of the canal are the femoral artery and vein, saphenous nerve and nerve to the vastus medialis muscle. The femoral artery and vein pass from the canal through the adductor hiatus to enter the popliteal fossa, becoming the popliteal artery and vein, respectively. The adductor longus is innervated by the obturator nerve, which does not travel within the adductor canal.
